correctness.rationale: For q any prime power and dimension d>=2, the affine nonsingular-symmetric graph transform sums f(x,Mx+c) over x for each invertible symmetric M and c. Its counting-norm Gram operator is translation invariant; at Fourier mode (alpha,beta) the eigenvalue is q^d times the number of invertible symmetric M with M beta=-alpha. The constant mode has q^d S_d, while exactly 2(q^d-1) coordinate-axis nonconstant modes have eigenvalue zero. For alpha,beta nonzero, imposing a nonzero dot product gives S_{d-1} matrices, while dot=0 gives q^{d-1} S_{d-2} matrices by a congruence/Schur complement calculation. Their frequencies have multiplicities (q^d-1)(q-1)q^{d-1} and (q^d-1)(q^{d-1}-1), respectively. The two positive nonconstant modes coincide iff d is odd; for even d their ratio gives singular-value condition (1-q^{1-d})^-1/2. The kernel is exactly zero-mean row-only plus column-only functions. Independent full frequency incidence census for (q,d)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2) reproduced eigenvalues, ranks, multiplicities and kernel counts. The theorem concerns the restricted invertible-symmetric graph family, not all Lagrangian views.

originality.rationale: The full continuous real Lagrangian Radon transform of Marmo–Michor–Neretin integrates over all affine Lagrangians and develops symplectic inversion, not an exact finite-field spectrum for invertible symmetric graph slopes. Doowon Koh obtains finite-field L^p->L^r endpoint estimates for broader X-ray/Radon views, not this restricted graph-family Gram matrix or parity-tuned stability. Standard counts of nonsingular symmetric matrices (Brent–McKay) supply necessary arithmetic, not the incidence-conditioned Fourier multiplicities. Scarabotti studies multiplicity-free permutation representations; its complete text could not be accessed, and the abstract alone cannot exclude an implicit stronger transform theorem. With this explicit priority risk, the restricted-view kernel, exact Fourier spectrum and odd/even tightness are best-of-knowledge original.
